## Root cause

The pagination contract is a cursor over the `(createdAt, id)` tuple, but only `createdAt` was actually used:

- `compareRows` tied on `createdAt` and returned `0`, so `sortRows` had no deterministic id tiebreaker.
- `encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor` dropped the `id` and reconstructed the position as `{ createdAt, id: '' }`.
- `isAfter` compared only `row.createdAt > position.createdAt`.

So when a page boundary landed in the middle of a batch sharing one millisecond, every remaining row in that millisecond compared *not greater* than the cursor's timestamp and was filtered out on the next page — silently lost. Insertions/deletions of rows in that same bucket then changed which tied rows survived, making the loss look like shifting.

export function toCamel(key) {

  // the separator pass can title-case each word (LINE_TOTAL -> lineTotal).
  const folded = text === text.toUpperCase() ? text.toLowerCase() : text
  return folded.replace(/[-_]+([a-zA-Z0-9])/g, (whole, char) => char.toUpperCase())
}
